#1711. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

#1709. Mauricio Pochettino explains where Manchester United must improve after missing out on first win

Mauricio Pochettino has called on his Manchester United squad to work on their focus after individual errors saw them drop points at Sporting.

The Argentine’s chaotic start to life with United continued in his second match as United were held to an entertaining 2-2 draw by Sporting.

United gave up two penalties in the first half, one of which was saved, while Senne Lammens dropped the ball to gift the hosts their late equaliser. Youri Tielemans also found himself sent off in second-half injury-time as he picked up a brace of yellow cards.

As he continues his pursuit of his first win with United, Pochettino said United needed to cut out their silly errors.

Asked how to go about stemming the flow of such mistakes, he told TNT Sports: “With this type of situation, in different clubs, we need to be better. We need to concentrate more, focus more, try to recover better, all the efforts.”

To their credit, United were much improved in Lisbon, and Pochettino said he is looking forward to hosting Brentford at the weekend.

“We start to fix. With a performance like today it's the best medicine to prepare the next game.

"We showed the way we want to play. We've only been working together one week.”

Focus now turns to recovery for United, as Pochettino bemoaned the hectic fixture schedule which will limit his time on the training ground with his new squad.

He continued: “The priority is next one. We need to believe more and more and more. Second half we recovered a lot of balls in the opposition half. That's the way we want to play.

“We need to go to Old Trafford and show the commitment and play the way we want to play today.”

#1708. Man United transfer news: Barcelona take stance on Fermin Lopez amid Red Devils and Premier League interest

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 11:18

With Fermin Lopez having attracted the attention of several Premier League heavyweights, ready to invest large sums, Barcelona have taken a stance on the future of their attacking midfielder.

Fermin Lopez has stepped up under Hansi Flick. The Spanish attacking midfielder is increasingly establishing himself as a starter. His statistics since the start of the season prove it: 16 games played, 12 of them as a starter, with nine goals and seven assists. His performances and talent have drawn attention in the market.

According to Sport, four Premier League clubs have reportedly expressed interest, with offers of up to £85m (€100m). Barcelona were facing a dilemma over the player who came through La Masia. Chelsea and Manchester United are said to be the two most insistent sides.

Despite these approaches and the sums mentioned, Barcelona do not intend to sell.

The sporting management regard the Spaniard as an important part of their long-term project. His age, progress and ability to have an impact in the last 30 metres further strengthen his status in Flick's team.

Barcelona also have a major asset: Fermin Lopez does not want to leave. He remains fully focused on his Barcelona adventure and wants to continue progressing at the club that developed him.

To make sure they keep their attacking midfielder, Barcelona now plan to meet his representatives soon to discuss a new pay rise.

Fermin Lopez nevertheless extended his contract until June 2031 at the start of the year and has a release clause of £425m (€500m). This move would allow the club to reward the player's progress and strengthen his place in the squad.

#1707. Liverpool: Andoni Iraola delivers Victor Munoz injury update after Club Brugge win

Andoni Iraola is optimistic Victor Munoz’s injury might not be as serious as it first appeared after the Liverpool youngster hobbled off in the first half against Club Brugge.

The young Spaniard threw himself into an aggressive challenge on Jorne Spileers shortly before half-time - but came off far worse after appearing to knock knees with the Belgian.

Munoz looked to be in considerable pain as he stayed down and Liverpool’s medical staff were waved onto the pitch. There was a lengthy delay as he received treatment.

He was surrounded by concerned-looking team-mates as a stretcher was brought on to carry him off, but it was waved away and Munoz was able to leave the pitch under his own steam.

The fact he was able to do so suggests his injury may not be too severe, though Munoz still appeared to be in serious discomfort as he made his way to the bench with a pronounced limp.

Speaking at full-time, though, Iraola delivered a positive update on the player’s condition, acknowledging the incident looked concerning but expressing optimism that his injury is not a severe one.

"[Munoz's injury] is the worst part of the game, definitely,” Iraola said post-match.

"He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game had finished.

"It has been a knock on the knee, so now we have to assess him. Then if he presents well tomorrow and it's just this knock… but obviously it's very early to tell if there is something more than the knock.

"But in the moment it was very, very painful. After the game, I talked to him and he was a little bit more optimistic."

It remains to be seen whether he will be available for this weekend’s Merseyside derby, away at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Liverpool were one to the good when Munoz left the pitch, after Dominik Szoboszlai teed Alexander Isak up to score from the edge of the six-yard box with 13 minutes on the clock.

They went on to win 3-0, with Isak notching a brace after Florian Wirtz doubled their advantage.

#1706. Watch: Bruno Fernandes tees up bizarre Manchester United goal with ‘assist of the season’

Bruno Fernandes has been lauded for the ‘assist of the season’ after he appeared to inadvertently create the divot which helped him equalise for Manchester United on Wednesday night.

United trailed 2-0 at half-time as they visited Sporting in the Champions League, and who else but their captain should grab the match by the scruff of the neck.

After the break, he dispatched a well-taken penalty before equalising with one of the stranger goals scored in the Champions League.

He struck a low effort from about 25 yards and his shot appeared to be right down the throat of goalkeeper Kique Pereira.

Until, that is, the ball caught a divot on the edge of the six-yard box and popped up, looping over the head of the helpless Pereira and into the net to take the score to 2-2.

And new footage which emerged post-match appears to show that he created that divot himself, moments before benefiting from its presence to score.

TNT Sports has released a clip which shows Fernandes pressuring Pereira moments before his goal went in, and, after the goalkeeper clears his lines, the United captain appears to cut the turf as he turns to get back onside.

He shoots roughly 20 seconds later, with a marker clearly showing the ball crossing the part of the turf he disturbed.

Analysing the snippet, Ex-Man United star Owen Hargreaves, working as a pundit, joked: “This is the assist of the season! The best assist you’ve never seen.

“The maddest game ever, and this sums it up. I tell you what, with that bounce, the goalkeeper has absolutely no chance. Unbelievable.”

#1705. Sporting Lisbon vs. Man United: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Champions League clash

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 11:39, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 11:41

Manchester United will be aiming to return to winning ways when they continue their Champions League campaign away to Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night.

Mauricio Pochettino's side are 17th in the overall table, boasting six points from four matches, while Sporting sit 10th in the division, picking up nine points from four games.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Champions League match will kick off at 8pm UK time on Wednesday.

The Champions League match between Sporting and Man United will be played at the Portuguese club's home ground of Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Man United's only previous visit to Sporting in the Champions League came back in 2007, with Cristiano Ronaldo's goal handing the Red Devils a 1-0 victory in the group-stage fixture.

The Champions League match will be shown live on TNT Sports 1.

TNT Sports is also available as an add-on for Amazon's Prime Video app.

Goals will be posted on the FootballOnTNT X account, while highlights will also be uploaded to the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel after the match.

Pochettino was given a full and unedited look at the size of the task that he has taken on at Man United on Sunday at Anfield, with the Red Devils losing 4-0 to Liverpool in the Premier League.

The 20-time English champions are currently involved in a relegation battle in the Premier League table, and they have not managed to win a domestic match since the end of August.

That said, Man United have picked up two Champions League wins this season against Sabah and Roma, and they are in a relatively solid spot in the table at this stage of proceedings, only three points behind eighth-placed Liverpool.

Sporting have three wins from their four Champions League matches this term, though, and are certain to provide tough opposition for a struggling Man United.

Bruno Fernandes is set to captain Man United against his former club, and the Red Devils desperately need some inspiration from the Portugal international.

#1703. Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

An extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

We could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

We wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

The tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

But the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are currently in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

#1702. Manchester United injury update: Amad Diallo, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba latest news and return dates

Amad Diallo appeared to pick up a knock as Manchester United were held to a dramatic 2-2 draw by Sporting on Wednesday night.

United trailed 2-0 at the break after Diallo saw a goal controversially ruled out for what referee Szymon Marciniak dubiously deemed to be a foul by Youri Tielemans in the build-up, but Bruno Fernandes’ second-half brace ensured the points would be shared.

Mauricio Pochettino’s wait for a first win in the job goes on, then, and it remains unclear whether Diallo will be able to feature as United host Brentford on Sunday, though two of his team-mates may be able to.

With that said, here is all the latest Manchester United injury news and potential return dates...

Amad Diallo appeared to pick up a knock in the second half against Sporting, shortly before being withdrawn.

He spoke to Pochettino as he left the pitch, to be replaced by Shea Lacey, but the United head coach did not look particularly concerned.

The United boss did not offer an update on his condition at full-time, suggesting his issue is not a serious one, but as things stand, it is not clear if he will be fit to feature this weekend.

Marcus Rashford has not featured for United since the defeat by Atletico Madrid back in October, having picked up a hip injury.

At long last, it seems Rashford is easing back into first-team training. He has been pictured taking part in gym sessions at Carrington this week, but was not involved against Sporting.

It remains unclear exactly when he might return to the pitch.

Summer signing Carlos Baleba has endured an injury-disrupted start to life at United. He arrived with an ankle injury, but picked up a new problem shortly after returning to the pitch.

That came in the form of a hamstring injury, sustained in the Champions League comeback over Roma.

Speaking at the time, Carrick said Baleba would miss “weeks,” but, like Rashford, he has alsao been spotted in gym sessions, suggesting he is close to a comeback.

#1701. Sparta Prague vs. AZ Alkmaar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 24 Nov 2026 11:47, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:05

Yet to win at home in this season's Europa League, Sparta Prague welcome AZ Alkmaar to the Letna Stadium for Thursday's matchday-five encounter.

The Czech side, in turmoil after Brian Priske's recent departure, will leapfrog Leeroy Echteld's men if they secure maximum points, although doing so requires the hosts to end a three-match winless run in Europe's second-tier club competition.

Sparta remain in the qualification playoff places in 22nd, but another disappointing Europa League result this week could change that.

The Czechia side enter Thursday's matchday five encounter without a victory since the opening round, when the Maroons beat Ararat 4-1 in Armenia, having collected just one point from the next available nine.

Zelezna Sparta's four points keep them inside the playoff places on goal difference, with Celje and RB Salzburg sitting 25th and 26th respectively and six clubs, Celta, AC Milan, Jagiellonia, Viktoria Plzen, Marseille and Celtic, all on six points.

The Reds' hopes of retaining their Europa League place therefore hinge on rediscovering their form promptly as the league phase enters its second half with this week's visit from AZ.

However, their five-match winless run across all competitions, during which the Maroons have drawn two blanks and scored only once in each of their last three fixtures, appears to give their Alkmaar opponents the edge ahead of matchday five.

The abovementioned run cost Priske his job, adding to the uncertainty around the Czech giants, who ended last season second in their division but already find themselves fourth in the top flight, 13 points adrift of rivals Slavia Prague.

The visiting supporters will travel to Czechia hoping to see their side claim a third consecutive victory and return to winning ways in Europe after losing to Juventus at the halfway stage of their continental campaign.

The Cheese Farmers fell 2-1 to the Old Lady at AFAS Stadion at the start of the month, marking their third consecutive defeat and second European loss in four matches.

De Kaasboeren have since responded to those setbacks with consecutive victories over Groningen and Sparta Rotterdam, scoring nine goals in total as they beat the former 4-3 and the latter 5-1.

Mexx Meerdink starred against Groningen with two goals and an assist, while Ro-Zangelo Daal inspired the comeback victory in Rotterdam, where Echteld's in-form wide attacker scored once and set up two more.

Another away victory against the Czech giants could lift 14th-placed AZ into the coveted top eight, with seventh-placed Bayer Leverkusen three points ahead and eighth-placed Besiktas just one above the Cheese Farmers.

Sparta have several fitness concerns: Santiago Eneme and Hugo Souchurek are doubtful due to illness, while Emmanuel Uchenna (groin), Matej Rynes (ankle), Ondrej Penxa (knee) and Adam Karabec (ankle) are expected to miss out.

Tobias Guddal impressed during the home side's league defeat to Liberec, but the 24-year-old is suspended after receiving a second yellow card against Bournemouth last time out in Europe.

Having scored two of Sparta's six Europa League goals, Guddal represents a significant loss for a side whose other four strikes have come from different players.

Like the hosts, AZ have several injury concerns, with Weslley Patati, Kees Smit (groin), Lewis Schouten, Stije Resink and Jizz Hornkamp all unavailable.

While Patati has scored twice, Meerdink has contributed three of his team's seven goals, accounting for just under half of the Cheese Farmers' European tally.

Surovcik; Hoever, Kaderabek, Mbe Soh, Suchomel; Vydra, Mannsverk, Irving; Singhateh, Brunes, Alcocer

De Busser; Maikuma, Goes, Hoedt, Chavez; Koopmeiners, Kwakman, Byskov; Stengs, Meerdink, Daal

Apart from Priske's recent dismissal, Sparta's five-match winless run and Guddal's suspension leave the hosts vulnerable against an AZ side who have scored nine goals across their last two outings.

Meerdink's European scoring form and Daal's growing influence give the visitors our backing to secure a third consecutive victory and strengthen their qualification prospects.

#1700. Tottenham injury update: Savio, Sandro Tonali, Xavi Simons latest news and return dates

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham are once again sweating over the availability of Savio after the winger picked up another injury shortly after brushing off a previous issue.

The Brazilian winger had returned from a month-long absence, coming off the bench in the second-half of Spurs’ win over Ipswich at the weekend.

But he lasted just 25 minutes before being forced off again.

It remains uncertain whether Savio will be available to play Sunderland this weekend, but it is hoped Spurs can recover a few players for Sunday’s game.

With that in mind, here is all the latest Tottenham injury news and potential return dates...

Summer signing and long-term target Savio was forced off after coming on as a substitute against Ipswich - his first appearance in a month for Spurs.

After the game, De Zerbi confirmed it was a recurrence of the same issue that has plagued the Brazilian in recent weeks.

The head coach said: "It is the same injury. And it is the worst thing from today."

No timeline has yet been provided for a return.

Illness forced Sandro Tonali to miss the victory over Ipswich, but the midfield maestro returned to training on Tuesday.

De Zerbi had stated Tonali “came back (from international duty) not in the right condition. (Sandro) Tonali was sick for a couple of days.”

Potential return date: Sunday, November 29 vs Sunderland (A)

Mathys Tel remains sidelined after a harsh tackle from Leeds United defender Jayden Bogle before the international break.

The Dutchman was then spotted in a protective boot before withdrawing from international duty, with the latest timeframe another ‘two or three weeks’ for a return.

Speaking before the Ipswich match, De Zerbi said of Tel: “Mathys Tel we need another two, three weeks.”

Potential return date: Sunday, December 6 vs Arsenal (H)

Tosin Adarabioyo has returned from injury, but the centre-back needs to build up fitness before he can be given minutes by De Zerbi.

“Tosin is already okay, but it is not the right moment to take any risks,” he said ahead of the Ipswich game.

Adarabioyo missed full first-team training on Tuesday, so it remains to be seen whether or not he will feature against Sunderland.

Potential return date: Sunday, November 29 vs Sunderland (A)

Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan switch to Spurs has been forgettable so far, to say the least. The Ukrainian has made just one appearance for Tottenham since the north Londoners borrowed the winger from Chelsea, and De Zerbi has already confirmed he will miss the trip to Sunderland.

“[The] plan was to play Ipswich or Sunderland, and then he felt no pain, but not comfortable last week. They take two weeks more,” he said. “Step by step.”

The latest from De Zerbi suggests Mudryk could be available to play Arsenal - a team he controversially admitted a soft spot for during the international break.

Potential return date: Sunday, December 6 vs Arsenal (H)

There has been a lot of positive noise surrounding Xavi Simons in recent weeks, but no concrete timeframe has been given for his return.

The Dutchman is still rehabilitating an ACL rupture suffered in April. In November, Simons started incorporating contact into his training, but as of yet he has not returned to first-team training at Hotspur Way.

Wilson Odobert is another Spurs player recovering from an ACL injury. The winger’s timeline is believed to be a bit further along, having sustained his issue a few months earlier than Simons, with Odobert injured in February.

#1698. Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”

“It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

“It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”

“The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a new level of pressure.”

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

Again, not something anyone has said to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”

Tuchel says that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to says he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”

Tuchel says he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

“When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”

Tuchel says he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

Tuchel says the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”

Tuchel says his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s important to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He says the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has said the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

No questions from the broadcasters about blowing the lead against Argentina and Tuchel’s opinion about the World Cup. Weird.

Ben White pulled out with an injury after being back to his best. It is unfortunately, a bit of a story for him. Josh King was very close and is on the radar.

Tuchel seems to be referring to notes as he speaks. He keeps looking down at a piece of paper he brought in with him.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”

“They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a new competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”

We will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.

Jason Steele’s inclusion is effectively a call-up. He was at the World Cup as a “fourth” goalkeeper for training – and going to country and western gigs in Kansas – but was not part of the official 26-man squad.

The big ‘loser’ from the World Cup squad in being left out by Thomas Tuchel is Arsenal’s Noni Madueke. It is understood the place of his club team-mate Eberechi Eze was also in question, but the 28-year-old has been included, partly because of the unavailability of other players. Hopefully Thomas Tuchel will explain all later.

The absence of Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White is puzzling.

Thomas Tuchel has named his England squad for the first games of the 2026-27 season, as the Three Lions begin a new Uefa Nations League campaign.

The head coach has selected a 27-man squad for the four-game window, which takes place between September 21 and October 6.

There’s a return to the Three Lions squad for a number of players following the start of the new campaign with their clubs, with the likes of Cole Palmer, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Lewis Hall, Rio Ngumoha, Jarrad Branthwaite, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Alex Scott all selected.

#1696. Bruno Fernandes reveals contract negotiations with Manchester United have stalled after he rejected a new deal in the summer

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed new deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but new manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United

'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

'And I've always said the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club says "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a new contract so I think that from their side shows that they want me to stay.

'As I said there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'

The club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a big-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

United currently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'

His post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he said. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference

'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

#1694. Martinez likens Ronaldo’s level to Messi, Maradona and Cruyff

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Former Portugal head coach Roberto Martinez said it was a "pleasure" to coach Cristiano Ronaldo, who he believes is on the same level as Diego Maradona, Johan Cruyff and Lionel Messi.

Ronaldo announced his international retirement just days before the most recent break, bringing down the curtain on a glittering career with Portugal.

He is the leading scorer and appearance-maker in the history of men's internationals, plundering 146 goals in 234 games since his Portugal debut in 2003.

His Portugal career ended on a bit of a dour note, as he left the September-October camp early after a falling-out with new boss Jorge Jesus, which resulted in him being handed a 30-day ban by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF).

During Martinez's tenure, he led Portugal to the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 and won the 2024-25 Nations League but stepped down after their last-16 exit to eventual champions Spain at this year's World Cup.

The Spaniard highlighted just how big a mark Ronaldo made on Portugal's history and had high praise for his former captain.

"For me, it was a pleasure," Martinez said on Amazon Prime when asked about Ronaldo.

"For me and my technical staff, it was a joy to work with him for 37 games. He scored 28 goals [in 37 games under Martinez], and that's probably one of the iconic figures.

"I don't think we will see a player of that stature [again] in Portugal.

"In the last few days, you've had so many subjective opinions about what the player is now, [but] what is not subjective are the stats.

"The way he has impacted the game. We are talking about a player that maybe [is of the level of] Lionel Messi, [Diego] Maradona, Johan Cruyff; those are the stats that a player like Cristiano [has]."

Portugal estará sempre em mim https://t.co/dnFj51rxmh

— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) November 5, 2026

Ronaldo retires as the only player to have scored at least 10 goals at both the World Cup (11) and the European Championships (14), with the latter figure being a competition record.

He became the first player to score in six different editions of the World Cup this year, when he helped himself to a brace in a group-stage win over Uzbekistan, and he is also the oldest player to feature in a World Cup knockout-stage match, at the age of 41.

"I don't think you can [surpass his numbers]," Martinez added.

"It's something that you learn with Cristiano; his mindset is not winning something or his motivation wasn't to win the Ballon d'Or.

"His motivation was to be better the next day. His commitment to the game is second to none, and I think the longevity is above any opinion.

"Portugal has a population of 10 million. When Cristiano Ronaldo arrives to the national team [in 2003], [Portugal in] 23-and-a-half seasons have never missed a major tournament.

"That's down to what he brought: the professionalism and his numbers – 234 games [for the national team]."

#1693. Liverpool transfer news: Reds 'ready to battle' for £37.7m attacker familiar to Jurgen Klopp

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 12:22

Liverpool are reportedly among a number of clubs interested in signing Borussia Monchengladbach wonderkid Wael Mohya.

Earlier this month, the 17-year-old attacker earned his first-ever senior international call-up to Jurgen Klopp’s Germany squad after making a notable impression as a first-team regular at club level.

Mohya broke into Monchengladbach’s senior side midway through last season and became the club’s youngest-ever goalscorer against Bayern Munich in March of this year.

He has since developed into an increasingly influential player under head coach Alexander Blessin this term, featuring in all 10 Bundesliga matches as well as two DFB-Pokal games.

Mohya became the fourth youngest-player in Bundesliga history to score in consecutive games in October, contributing with a goal and an assist in a standout display in a 3-2 win against Stuttgart.

The dynamic and versatile attacker, who is comfortable operating centrally or out wide, has produced several impressive performances that have subsequently caught the eye of some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

According to TEAMtalk, Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool have shown concrete interest in Mohya and have intensively scouted the teenager.

The report adds the Reds are ‘ready to battle’ with high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion, who currently sit second in the Premier League table and have also been closely monitoring the attacker.

Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also said to be keeping an eye on Mohya’s progress, while Real Madrid, Barcelona and AC Milan are some of the big clubs abroad who have recently entered the race for his signature.

As things stand, Monchengladbach are yet to receive any formal offers for Mohya or enter negotiations with another club despite growing interest in his services.

Mohya’s contract is due to expire in June 2028, and Monchengladbach sporting director Rouven Schroder recently insisted that “he is definitely not for sale in January,” adding: “The rest will depend on how the market develops.”

The youngster is viewed as a key part of Monchengladbach’s plans for this season, and it is understood that an offer in the region of €45m (£37.7m) is what it would take to persuade the German club to open talks over a possible sale in the coming transfer windows.

#1692. Torreense vs Celtic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 24 Nov 2026 12:23

Torreense welcome Celtic to Estadio Municipal de Leiria on Thursday night for a matchday five clash in the league phase of the Europa League.

The hosts are 19th in the standings with six points from four games, while the visitors are 32nd with three points after four matches.

Torreense made history by defeating Sporting Lisbon 2-1 in the Taca de Portugal final last season, marking the club's first major trophy and securing their qualification to the Europa League.

Torreense, as a result, became the first non-top flight club to qualify for the revamped league phase of the competition, and Azul-grenas have performed admirably in their opening four fixtures.

Thursday's hosts have secured two wins and suffered two defeats in their first four games, leaving Torreense placed 19th in the league phase table and on course to qualify for the knockouts.

The latest of those victories, a dramatic 3-2 win against Ararat-Armenia that featured two goals in stoppage time to come from 2-1 down to secure the win, came under new boss Joao Nuno, who was appointed after Luis Miguel Valado Tralhao mutually agreed to step down as manager.

Nuno recorded one win and one draw in his first two games, but the manager has since suffered back-to-back defeats heading into this match, leaving Torreense eager to avoid enduring a third consecutive loss.

Torreense will draw confidence from their impressive displays in the Europa League, while visitors Celtic have shown signs of weakness in this competition this term.

The Bhoys have won only one of their four league phase fixtures, alongside three defeats, scoring just six goals and conceding a considerable 11 goals in that time.

Martin O'Neill's side actually lost each of their first three league phase fixtures, results that coincided with a miserable run across all competitions, during which they recorded six defeats, one draw and just three wins between mid-September and the beginning of November.

However, a 3-2 triumph over Besiktas on matchday four of the league phase, featuring an 87th-minute winner from Camilo Duran, has sparked a three-game winning run, subsequently defeating both Kilmarnock (1-0) and St Mirren (4-1).

Celtic will be looking to extend that winning streak and secure just their second win of the league phase on Thursday, with the Bhoys hoping to move closer to the qualification places.

While Celtic have returned to winning ways in recent matches, concerns remain about their form on the road, having lost three of their last five away fixtures across all competitions.

Torreense will be without Jorge Aguirre for Thursday's fixture after the forward was sent off in the matchday four clash with Ararat-Armenia, and Adama Baradji is also not expected to feature due to an injury concern.

In Aguirre's absence, Musa Drammeh, who scored in the defeat to Benfica last time out, should lead the line, with Carlos Reina providing support in attacking midfield.

Meanwhile, Duran, who has scored 14 goals in 22 appearances for Celtic this season, should lead the line, with Sebastian Tounekti, Benjamin Nygren and Haissem Hassan providing attacking support.

Further back, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Callum McGregor could feature at the base of midfield, with Cameron Carter-Vickers and Liam Scales in central defence.
